## 389. The attract playlist is data a title ships; the port's is an expression

Section 388 asked for the playlist, so the playlist was read where it lives. The title screen's code
does not build a name: it indexes a **list of names in the executable** and copies that string into
the load buffer. Each title's own list, from `tools/th-demo-lists.py` (a PE walk: the string pool,
then the run of consecutive pointers into it), beside the demos the title ships and the stage each of
those demos records (through the parse that mirrors the port's load path):

| title | ships, with the stage it records | the executable's own list (first three) | their stages |
| ----- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| th12 | demo0.rpy=4 demo1.rpy=3 demo2.rpy=1 demo3.rpy=1 | demo2.rpy(1), demo1.rpy(3), demo0.rpy(4) | 1 3 4 |
| th13 | demo0.rpy=3 demo1.rpy=2 demo2.rpy=1 demo3.rpy=5 | demo2.rpy(1), demo1.rpy(2), demo0.rpy(3) | 1 2 3 |
| th14 | demo0.rpy=3 demo1.rpy=4 demo2.rpy=1 | demo0.rpy(3), demo1.rpy(4), demo2.rpy(1) | 3 4 1 |
| th16 | demo1.rpy=3 demo2.rpy=1 demo3.rpy=2 demo4.rpy=4 | demo1.rpy(3), demo2.rpy(1), demo3.rpy(2) | 3 1 2 |
| th17 | demo1.rpy=3 demo2.rpy=4 demo3.rpy=2 | demo1.rpy(3), demo2.rpy(4), demo3.rpy(2) | 3 4 2 |
| th18 | demo1.rpy=3 demo2.rpy=2 demo3.rpy=4 demo4.rpy=1 | demo1.rpy(3), demo2.rpy(2), demo3.rpy(4) | 3 2 4 |

The code that consumes the list, per title (`cmp <idle counter>, 0x708`, `inc`, a key test, then
`mov reg, [index*4 + list]`, a string copy, and the load call):

    th16  index read at 0x44afd1 (va), list use at 0x44afd6, index step at 0x44b000
    th17  the same code at 0x45169d, 0x4516a2, and the same step after it
    th12  index read at 0x43f79f, list use at 0x43f7a5, index step at 0x43f7de

`0x708` is 1800, so the port's threshold and the shape of the branch are right: the counter
increments once per title screen frame, any key resets it, and 1800 idle frames start a demo. The
step is a branchless remainder by three (`mov eax, 0x55555555 / imul / sub / sar 1 / add`), which
evaluates to `(index + 1) % 3`, and the index is a global whose only writers are that function - so
its shipped value is the start, and all three titles that carry it ship **zero**. A title's playlist
is therefore `list[0], list[1], list[2]`, then back to the beginning; th16 and th18 name a fourth
demo that this path never reaches.

The port plays a different playlist, measured three ways in one place (`GameSession.cpp:182`):
`"demo" + char('3' - (demo_index++ & 3)) + ".rpy"` - four names counted down, starting at
`demo3`. Against the titles:

* the names are th12's (it is the only shape for which `demo0` is a shipped name, and even there
  the executable's list is `demo2, demo1, demo0`, not `demo3` first);
* the steps after the first walk into a file the generation does not ship: nothing names
  `demo0.rpy` in th16, th17 or th18, and beyond the run the fourth demo step is
  `fail("original demo resource missing")` at `GameSession.cpp:183`;
* the walked evidence of section 388 shows the first demo of both titles at `stage=2` (that is
  th16's `demo3` and th17's `demo3`), where the titles' own lists start at `stage=3`
  (th16 `demo1`, th17 `demo1`).

So the next change is to transcribe the list instead of computing a name - three entries and their
order per title, `index = (index + 1) % 3`, start 0 - and it is checkable in the existing
instrument: after the change the first demo of th16 and of th17 is their own `demo1`, whose
recorded stage is 3, so the run's first demo visit must read `stage=3` where section 388's walked
`stage=2`. The runs of section 388 and their numbers stay as they are, as the before column.

## 390. The transform: the port plays the list a title ships, and the demo it plays owns the next wall

Sections 389 read both halves of the attract playlist out of the titles - which names an executable
stores, and which step its own code applies to the index - and this round transcribes them:

```cpp
struct DemoPlaylist { const char* names[4]; u32 step; };
// 12, 13: demo2, demo1, demo0 / 3        14: demo0, demo1, demo2 / 3
// 16: demo1..demo4 / 3     17: demo1, demo2, demo3 / 3     18: demo1..demo4 / 4
if(title_idle>=1800){const DemoPlaylist playlist=demo_playlist();
    const auto path=std::string(playlist.names[demo_index<playlist.step?demo_index:0]);
    demo_index=(demo_index+1)%playlist.step;
    if(!source->read(path,bytes))return fail("original demo resource missing");
    return begin_replay(*source,bytes.data(),u32(bytes.size()),0,true); }
```

Six steps read one by one in the titles' own code: th12, th13, th14 and th16 use the 0x55555555
sequence (`(index+1) % 3`, at th12 0x43f7de and th16 0x44b001), th17 an `idiv` by a literal three
(0x516c9-0x516db), th18 a masked remainder by four (`and ecx, 3` at 0x64fd0). The lists themselves
are one command to reproduce, `py -3 tools/th-demo-lists.py`, and the delivered port now carries them.

The verification took three boots of one artifact, and the difference between them is a finding of its
own. Booted at the plain URL, the same build behaved as the code from before the edit - a four-name
countdown - and reported the same numbers as section 388; booted at `?run=<ticks>`, it logs and plays
what the round wrote. So a boot that is meant to test what was just built has to name a different
runtime, and the tracked `tools/boot-title.ps1` now appends that per-run query (a long comment in it
records the measurement).

What the fresh boot prints, per title, with the wall behind the playlist:

    th14  [demo] list entry 0 of 3: demo0.rpy / loaded 7255 bytes / record stage 3, char 0,
          diff 0  ->  wall: battle update failed: -1001 ECL opcode 410 at time 0.000000, stage
          frame 61
    th16  [demo] list entry 0 of 3: demo1.rpy / loaded 6437 bytes / record stage 3, char 0,
          diff 0  ->  wall: battle update failed: -1001 invalid MSG entry, stage frame 11
    th17  no log line reached the console in 70 s, but the page's own probe reads stage 3, no error,
          stage frame 2082 - the same verdict from a second instrument

`[replay] demo: record stage 3` is the prediction of section 389 answered by the data the run loads:
the first demo of each of these three titles is the one their own list names, and the record inside
it says stage 3, where the countdown played stage 2 (th16, th17) or asked for a file the title does
not ship (th14, whose first demo used to stop before it began). Read the other way, the numbers are
the same: the port used to fail on `demo3.rpy` for th14 and now loads `demo0.rpy` of 7255 bytes.

The wall that the playlist was hiding is the demo's own stage: the port reaches `stage=3` under
`demo0`/`demo1` and then the table has no row - an MSG entry for th16, ECL opcode 410 for th14 (the
4xx band of the dispatch catalogue, whose rows section 302+ left open). Both are on the demo path
now, which means the next round has the ordinary shape again: read the opcode's own handler out of
the title's machine code, land the row, and re-run the same demo to see it clear.

The tracked boot tool was then used on itself: `py -3 tools/read-boot.py` on a 45 s run of th17 at
`?run=<ticks>` reads `stageMax=3`, `stages [0, 3]`, and the page probe reads stage 3 with no error,
so the tool the round changed boots the list the round wrote. One argument-binding measurement came out
of that: the titles are the first positional as a plain array, where a remaining-arguments array
had let a named `-Wait` take the second bare title (`13 18` bound as titles=[13], wait=18, and an
empty list boots nothing and still exits 0) - so the tracked tool now takes `13`, `-Titles 13,18`,
and `-Suffix=-long`.

## 391. The th14 constant-velocity record: 408 and 410 run the machine's own mode table

Section 390's boot stopped at `ECL opcode 410 at time 0.000000` in the th14 demo (stage frame 61),
and the demo's own record names the instruction: `st03.ecl`, block `0x4b7c`+`0x100` and
`0x5470`+`0x100`, opcode `0x19a` with `time=0`, length 32, four float parameters
`-0.000435, 0.017453, 0, 0`. The titles' own dispatcher sends `0x198` and `0x19a` to
**0x426a74** and `0x199` and `0x19b` to **0x426b7f** (`py -3 tools/th-ecl-dispatch.py th14 0x198
0x199 0x19a 0x19b`), which is the first thing to read in the machine inside 0x426a74:

    0x426a7e  mov eax, 0x198
    0x426a8a  lea esi, [edi + 0x88]
    0x426a90  cmp cx, ax
    0x426a93  je  +                  ; 0x198 -> the record at +0x88, everything else at +0xcc
    0x426a95  lea esi, [edi + 0xcc]

Four arguments follow (the resolver 0x483fc0, `push 0..3`), then the handler's own stores, which the
oracle below reads back one by one:

    [esi+0x34..0x3c] <- [esi+0x00..0x08]   unless (flags & 0xf) == 2      (0x26aef, the gate at 0x26ae4)
    [esi+0x18] <- arg1 (speed)             always                         (0x26b35)
    [esi+0x1c] <- arg0 (angle)            through 0x4154a0, which normalizes  (0x26b13 -> 0x4154e6)
    [esi+0x20] <- arg2 (radius)                                          (0x26b49)
    [esi+0x24] <- arg3 (radial velocity)                                 (0x26b5b)
    [esi+0x40] <- (flags & ~0xd) | 2                                      (0x26b6b)

`0x26b0e` compares the angle against the double `[0x4c1c78] = -999999.0`, and each of the four
stores keeps the record's current value when its argument is that sentinel - the same idiom the
port's 400/402 and 404/406 rows already carry. The tail is the part that decides the record's
position: `0x4180` calls **0x3df0**, which dispatches on the nibble the handler just set,
`eax = [ecx+0x40] & 0xf; if (eax > 4) goto snap; jmp [eax*4 + 0x404160]`, and the table at
0x404160 reads

    mode 0 -> 0x403e13   position += velocity, then 0x40dc        (the port's Movement::update)
    mode 1 -> 0x4040dc   the 1/100 snap alone
    mode 2 -> 0x403e43   p = polar(angle, radius); position = velocity + (p.x, p.y, 0); snap
    mode 3 -> 0x403eaf   the ellipse form (0x28/0x2c, not measured this round)
    mode 4 -> 0x403f67
    the snap itself: value = float(floor(float(value) * 100)) / 100, i.e. [0x4c1b54] = 100.0

So 0x426a74 installs a *constant-velocity* movement: the position seeds the velocity unless the record
already runs in mode 2, the four arguments overwrite speed, angle, radius and radial velocity, and the
nibble becomes 2. `0x3e43` then bakes one step of it out of the new fields - `polar` on the new
angle and radius, added to the six bytes of velocity - and the shared tail (0x23750) is the
coordinate sum the port already runs as `combine_movement`.

## 392. The sibling 0x426b7f: the same test avenue, and the wall behind the demo is no longer an opcode

Section 391 left the th14 demo stopping at `ECL opcode 411 at time 0.000000` in stage three, and the
title's own dispatcher sends both 409 (0x199) and 411 (0x19b) to the sibling of the handler it had
just transcribed: `py -3 tools/th-ecl-dispatch.py th14 0x198 0x199 0x19a 0x19b` pairs 0x198/0x19a
with 0x426a74 and 0x199/0x19b with **0x426b7f**. Read from the exe, the sibling opens with the
same select (`mov esi,0x199`, then `cmp cx,si` twice more) and picks three records, not one:

    0x26b84..95  the movement record: +0x88 when the opcode is 0x199, else +0xcc   -> [esp+0x28]
    0x26b99..bad the first interpolator:  +0x3f8 when 0x199, else +0x458            -> [esp+0x14]
    0x26bb1..b9  the second:            +0x488 when 0x199, else +0x4cc            (esi)

Two integer arguments follow (0x2c1d0 at 0x26c6e and 0x26c7b) and three float ones (0x2c230 at
0x26bc3, 0x26bd2 and 0x26be1). The float three are the ends of the two interpolator records under
the same -999999.0 double of 0x4c1c78 the 408 path uses - 0x26bf8 substitutes the record's own
+0x18, 0x26c35 its +0x20, 0x26c1d its +0x24 (the stack offsets shift with the pushes, which is the
whole reason the window has to be read with the calls in it) - and the integer one is tested at
0x26c8e, `test ecx,ecx; jg 0x26ca5`. Only a **positive** count reaches the movement:

    0x26d2b  eax = [edx+0x40]; and eax,0xfffffff2; or eax,2; mov [edx+0x40],eax   (mode nibble 2)
    0x26d37  call 0x4180    -> 0x3df0 -> 0x403e43: p = polar(angle, radius); position = velocity + p
    0x26d3e  call 0x23750   -> the coordinate sum of 0x400/0x402, the port's combine_movement

A non-positive count zeroes +0x28 and +0x3c of the select records (0x26c92, 0x26c99) and jumps
straight to the ECL tail at 0x29c28, so the frame sees nothing change. The demo's own record
settles the shape from the other side: both `0x19b` instructions of st03.ecl are
`length=36 params=5` with arguments `0x50, 0x0, 0x-368bdc10, 0x41800000, 0` (block 0x4b7c +0x120
and block 0x5470 +0x120), i.e. a count of **80**, and the port's `command` fixture now feeds five
arguments (20 bytes into an instruction of length 36) so `float_argument(3)` and the three
`+2..+4` reads land where the title's own five do.

row for each of the two opcodes comes out identical to the oracle's with exactly two rules - the
count must be positive, and then the movement record is the one for the opcode and the tail above

those are precisely the rows whose first argument is positive.

Then in the port. The transcription is another twenty lines of EnemyTh14Commands.cpp, written from

## 393. The per-frame half of the mode table: 0x4230d0, and the demo walks from frame 63 to 120

Section 392 ended with a named suspicion rather than an opcode: two frames after the 411 command the
demo's update failed with a message whose numbers (`opcode 0, time 0`) are what an **empty** error
record holds, and the only `-2` in that neighbourhood which records nothing on the script side is

handler had just written. This round measured the frame function itself and replaced the refusal.

The frame function is 0x4230d0, the one the oracle's earlier timelines already drive. Its opening is
the answer to "what is a frame": a current-to-previous copy (`movq xmm0,[edi+0x44]; movq [edi],
xmm0` and the thirteen dwords after it), then the interpolator gate at 0x423142 (`cmp dword ptr
[edi+0x3f0],0`, the +0x28 duration of the first Vec2 band at 0x3c8) and the per-record nibble test
at 0x42314f (`mov eax,[edi+0xc8]; and eax,0xf; cmp eax,2 / cmp eax,3`), before the normalize
loop at 0x42316a. The `[edi+0xc8]` is the *absolute* record's flag word (0x88+0x40), so the test
the frame function performs is the same nibble the commands write.

Measuring it needed no new instrument, only more rows of the one that exists. `tools/
th14-enemy-movement-native.py` now drives 0x4230d0 over two families of seeds - modes 0, 1 and 2 on
either record, and the 3/4 pair beside them - and records the whole 53-word image plus status per

    378 movement setters, 960 mode-zero frame states, 168 constant-velocity/mode records,
    772 mode-0/1/2 frame states, 886 mode-3/4 frame states observed.

`tools/tmp/fit2.py` then fitted those 772 frames on paper - the three rules below plus the tail
562 words of the previous kinds - and reproduces **772 of 772**, so the transcription that follows is

    nibble 0   velocity.x/velocity.y = polar(angle, speed*rate); position += velocity; snap x/y
    nibble 1   snap x/y only
    nibble 2   angle += speed*rate (normalized); radius += radial_velocity*rate;
               position = velocity + polar(angle, radius); snap x/y (z keeps velocity.z)

around a frame whose observable parts are: the current record takes `absolute + relative - current`

## 394. The handler the demo stopped on: 0x426960, 48 measured band sets, and frame 161

Section 393 ended with a wall that was finally an opcode: `ECL opcode 445 at time 0.000000`, with
the titles' dispatcher resolving 445 (0x1bd) - together with 0x1bf - to 0x426960. The pair shares group 42 of the movement dispatch. This round read the handler,
measured 48 seeds of it, fitted
them on paper, transcribed it, and the demo gained another forty-one frames.

The handler, read from the executable: `mov esi,0x1bd; lea eax,[edi+0x88]; cmp cx,si; je ...;
lea eax,[edi+0xcc]` picks the movement record (+0x88 for 0x1bd, +0xcc otherwise) and stores that
pointer at `[esp+0x28]`, then `lea esi,[edi+0x3f8]` ... `lea esi,[edi+0x458]` picks the *scalar
band* of the same choice - the first and the third of the four interpolation records the frame
function samples, and the same pair the sibling 0x426b7f fills. `push 2; call 0x483fc0` reads
float argument 2, `movss xmm0,[eax+0x18]` reads the record's speed into `[esp+0x10]`, `push 0;
call 0x483f30` reads integer argument 0 and `test eax,eax; jg` sends a non-positive duration down a
path that only stores `[esi+0x28]=0` and jumps to the ECL tail. Otherwise `push 1; call 0x483f30`
reads the mode, the audit lands in `[esp+0x48]`, and the block from 0x269e1 folds the float
argument through the -999999 double at 0x4c1c78: mode 7 takes 0.0 when the value is the sentinel,
every other mode takes the record's own speed, and a real value always survives. The stores are
`[esi+0x28]` duration, `[esi]` start (the record's speed), `[esi+0x2c]` mode, `[esi+8]`/`[esi
+0xc]` the cleared tangents, `[esi+4]` the folded end value, then `call 0x14350` (the timer), then
`and dword ptr [eax+0x40],0xfffffff0` - the movement nibble cleared, and nothing else in the state
touched.

The oracle grew a block of 48 band sets of exactly that shape (`tools/th14-enemy-movement-native.py`,
`bandSets`), each one a `configured` snapshot of all four bands plus a 40-frame run of 0x4230d0:
**48 band sets (1520 frames)**. `tools/tmp/fit445.py` predicted every store before the port was
touched and scored **48/48**, including the two things that are easy to get wrong: the guard nibble
is cleared only on the positive-duration path (a zero or negative duration leaves the record's nibble
alone), and a non-positive duration touches no other field. The transcription is forty lines of
`enemy_th14_movement_command`, and the check now says

    PASS: 378 setters, 960 linear frames, 432 interpolation timelines / 16621 frames,
          772 mode-table frames, 48 band sets, 168 constant-velocity records

The bands are compared field for field (`interpolation_value`) and the state dword for dword, so the
handler's duration, mode, start, end, both tangents and the nibble clear all match the retail
machine.

One process catch from this round, worth writing down because it silently corrupts measurement:

variable leaves the served files at the previous build, and the boot then reports the *previous*
wall - the first boot of this round showed the identical 120 and the identical 445 for exactly that

    run: 37 s, 262578 frames, stage 3, phase 1, stageFrame 161 (120 before this round),

    battle update failed: -1001 ECL opcode 700 at time 0.000000

Forty-one more frames, and the wall is a different kind of opcode: 700 (0x2bc) resolves to
**0x4285eb** and the demo's own record of it sits at block 0x584 +0x17c with `length=36`, `params=5`
and `refs=0x4` - the shape of a sub-routine call, not another setter. That is the next

## 395. The pair behind 700: the slot writers, and the layout they share with 702

Section 394 stopped on `ECL opcode 700 at time 0.000000`, the record at block 0x584 +0x17c with
`length=36 params=5 refs=0x4`. The dispatcher resolves 700 (0x2bc) to 0x4285eb and 701 (0x2bd) to
0x42864d. Both are short, and this round read them, measured them, and transcribed them.

The shape, from the machine: `push 0; call 0x2c1d0` reads integer argument 0 and uses it as a slot
index, and `lea esi,[eax*8]; sub esi,eax; shl esi,7` scales it by 0x380 - the same stride 0x2bc
and 0x2bd use. 0x2bc then reads four floats (`push 1`, `push 2`, `push 3`, `push 4` through
0x2c230) and stores them at `[esi+edi+0x5a0]`, `+0x5a4`, `+0x5a8` and `+0x8d8`; 0x2bd reads five
integers and stores them at `+0x8e8`, `+0x8ec`, `+0x8f0`, `+0x8f4` and `+0x8f8`. Relative to the
slot's own base that is +0, +4, +8, +0x338 for 0x2bc and +0x348 through +0x358 for 0x2bd. Neither
handler bounds the index, and there is no other write.

Measured first: the oracle grew a `slotRows` block of 24 rows of exactly these two ops (indices 0, 1,
2, 3 and 7; argument pools that cross the sign and the integer_pattern boundaries), and each row
captures the record's whole imaged state plus 54 slot words - six slots times the nine fields the two
handlers can reach, so a write to the wrong slot or the wrong stride shows up. `tools/tmp/fit700.py`
predicted every one of those words before the port was touched and scored **24/24**, and the check
that now runs the port says

    PASS: 378 setters, 960 linear frames, 432 interpolation timelines / 16621 frames,
          772 mode-table frames, 48 band sets, 24 slot rows / 1296 slot words,
          168 constant-velocity records

The transcription is a new sixteen-record array on the port's TH14 state (`th14_slots`, stride 0x380,
`static_assert(sizeof(EnemyState::Th14Slot)==0x380)`), the two `case`s in the state command's
switch, two new fixture exports (`state_command` routes through the state command with a real
environment and an argument count so 701's sixth word is inside the instruction, `slot_value` reads
a slot word), and the size assertions moved by 0x3800 with a comment saying why.

The layout is not a guess, and 702 is the independent witness: its handler at 0x428a49 (the demo's
next op) does `lea esi,[edi+0x5c0]; add esi,ecx` with the same `eax*0x380`, then
`mov ecx,0xc6; rep movsd` - a copy of 0x318 bytes out of the slot. 0x5c0 is exactly the slot's
+0x20 and 0x5c0+0x318 is exactly the +0x338 the 700 head sits in front of and the tail float
behind, so the machine's own next reader confirms both the stride and the field split this round
transcribed.

The demo, rebuilt into the served directory (`TH11_OUTPUT=artifacts/sdl3-th14`) and booted at a fresh
URL:

    run: 37 s, 262582 frames, stage 3, phase 1, stageFrame 161, pageErrors 0, consoleErrors 1
    battle update failed: -1001 ECL opcode 702 at time 0.000000

The frame counter stands still this time because 700 and 702 sit in the same block at the same time,
so the two ops are consumed inside one tick; what moved is the wall, from opcode 700 to opcode 702.
That record is at block 0x584 +0x260 with `length=20`, one parameter and `refs=0`, and its handler
opens with `push 0x354` / `call 0x8f980` (a memset of a stack buffer), reads integer argument 0,
scales it by 0x380, copies `mov ecx,0xc6; rep movsd` 0x318 bytes out of `edi+0x5c0+index*0x380`,
and then reads three twelve-byte records indexed the same way at `+0x3ea0`, `+0x3e98` and `+0x3dd8`
of a manager object, comparing one float against `[0x4c19e8]`. That is the next transcription, and
its opening copy is also the check on this round's stride.

keepers: `py -3 tools/th-replay-parse.py` (exit 0), `py -3 tools/th-demo-lists.py` (the six shipped

## 396. The first reader of the slot table: 0x428a49, 3408 measured request words, and the demo at frame 841

Section 395 left the demo on `ECL opcode 702 at time 0.000000`. The dispatcher resolves 702 (0x2be)
to 0x428a49, and 0x2be is the first handler that *reads* the table 700/701 fill. This round read it
whole, measured it against the machine, transcribed it, and watched the demo pass it.

The handler, from the bytes: `push 0x354` / `push 0` / `lea eax,[esp+0xb0]` / `call 0x8f980`
memsets a 0x354-byte request on the stack, `mov ecx,edi; call 0x2c1d0` reads integer argument 0,
`lea esi,[eax*8]; sub esi,eax; shl esi,7` scales it by the table's own 0x380 (the stride
section 395 measured), `mov ecx,0xc6; rep movsd` copies the slot's body - 0x318 bytes, from the
record's +0x20, source `edi + 0x5c0 + index*0x380` - into the request at +0x34, and then the named
stores fill the request around it: +0x0c from the record's +0x0c through the angle normalizer at
0x43590 (whose two constants, [0x4c1aa4] and [0x4c1ad0], are the same pi and 2pi the frame
function's loop at 0x42316a uses), the head triples at +0x10/+0x14/+0x18, +0x1c and +0x20 from the
record, the two words *before* the record at +0x24/+0x28 (in the sampled data the previous slot's
last two words; slot 0's page is zeroed), +0x2c from the record's +0x1c, bit 0 of +0x30, and
+0x34c/+0x350 from the record's +0x368/+0x36c. The request's first three floats are the one real
choice in the handler: 0x28a95 loads the *offset* triple's z and compares it with the constant at
[0x4c19e8] - its four bytes are 0x3f666666 - and `comiss`/`jbe` sends
`z <= that constant` to the branch that adds the entity's own position at +0x44/+0x48/+0x4c, while
`z` above it takes `base + offset` with the result's z forced to zero. The machine ends by calling
0x43a750 with the request (`push eax; push 0; call 0x43a750`); the command's entire input to the
spawner is that buffer, so that buffer is the command's output.

Measured first, and the oracle had to be extended for it: `0x43a750` is stubbed with `ret 8` and a
code hook records the pointer argument, so the JSON carries 16 case-702 rows with the whole request
(213 words each) plus the seeds the handler read - the 0x380-byte slot record, the two words before
it, and the two sixteen-triple tables at +0x3dd8 and +0x3e98. `tools/tmp/fit702.py` rebuilt every
one of the 16 requests from those seeds *before* the port was touched, and it scored **16/16** -
after the machine corrected two of my readings: the two words at +0x24/+0x28 come from before the
record rather than from inside it, and the branch constant is 0.9 (0x3f666666), not a guess.
A provenance pass (a scratch resolver that maps each request word back to its source across the seeds)
is what found the first of those, and it also fixed the store at +0x2c, which is written *after*
the two pushes at 0x28c25/0x28c26 and so lands at +0x2c rather than +0x34.

## 397. The last writer of the record: 0x427ba9, and the port's duplicated slot view collapsed into the machine's own emitter

Section 396 left the demo on `ECL opcode 601 at time 0.000000`. The dispatcher resolves 601 (0x259)
to `0x427ba9`, and this round read that handler, measured it, and transcribed it. Doing so settled a
larger thing than the opcode: the array the port called the slot table was the same memory as the
emitter record the TH14 emitter model already had.

The handler, from the bytes. It opens with the same argument accessor the round-396 handler uses
(`push 0; mov ecx,edi; call 0x2c1d0`), scales the result by the same stride (`lea esi,[eax*8]; sub
esi,eax; shl esi,7`), and reads the *second* triple at `[edi + ecx*4 + 0x3ea0]` - that is the
triples at +0x3e98 with the stride folded in - comparing its z with the constant at `[0x4c19e8]`
whose four bytes are `0x3f666666`. `comiss` follows, and `jbe` sends "at or below" to the branch
that takes the entity's own +0x44/+0x48/+0x4c; the other branch takes `base + offset` - the +0x3dd8
triples plus the +0x3e98 ones - with the sum's z forced to zero. Both branches then
`lea edx,[eax+edi]` (the stride again, with *no* +0x598 in the address arithmetic), store the
result into `[edx+0x5a0]` and `[edx+0x5a8]`, set `[global+0x60] = [edi+0x4068]`, and call the
spawner `0x191a0` through `lea eax,[edx+0x598]; push eax`, clearing the global slot again after it.

The `+0x598` in that pointer is the whole round. It is where `Th14BulletEmitter` already says the
port's emitter array lives ("Native TH14 0x380-byte emitter at enemy +598"), and the handler itself
addresses the record *without* it and adds it once, at the call: **the record base is 0x598, not
0x5a0**. Section 394 modelled the table 700/701 write as `Th14Slot` based at 0x5a0, and section 396
added `th14_slot_prefix[8]` to make the "two words before the record" read defined. Both were an
8-byte shift of the record the port already had: the native +0x5a0 is that record's `position`,
+0x5c0 is its `transforms`, +0x340 is its `values_340`, +0x598/+0x59c are the `sprite` and the
`color` the emitter's own header names. So 700 writes the emitter's position and its first
`values_340` word, 701 writes `values_340[4..8]`, and 702's "two words before the record" are the
record's own first two words at +0x24/+0x28.

Measured before touching the port, and both halves of the handler are in the machine's own numbers:
the oracle now drives `0x427ba9` over 16 rows with the spawner stubbed (`ret 4`) and a code hook
recording the pointer, and `docs/porting/enemy-movement-native.json` carries `fireRows` with each row's
pre-record, its whole post-record (0x380 bytes) and the spawner's argument. `tools/tmp/fit601.py`
rebuilt every row's head from the seeds alone and scored **16/16**, and every recorded pointer came
back as `record base` - the native +0x598 + index*0x380, exactly, for indices 0, 1, 2, 3 and 7.

The port now keeps one array instead of two. `Th14Slot th14_slots[16]`, `th14_slot_prefix[8]` and
the twice-role-named `th14_emitter_offsets/origins[16]` are gone; the emitter record is the single
0x380-byte view, and the two native triples stay as `th14_base_vectors`/`th14_offset_vectors`
because 603 and 628 write them. The state's size assertion moves by the request alone
(`+0x354`); the compiler's own message is the check on that arithmetic. 601's rule is an inline
`enemy_th14_fire_position` (the only part of the handler the port can act on before the spawner) and
the command keeps calling the port's spawner, which is where the demo's wall now is:

    PASS: 378 setters, 960 linear frames, 432 interpolation timelines / 16621 frames,

The check seeds each fire row's own pre-record and tables, runs the position rule, and compares the
**whole 0x380-byte record** word for word on all 16 rows - so a write anywhere else in the record
would fail it, not just the position.
